title: Failed pump leaves community struggling with water supply problems for weeks
text:
ATASCOSA - Thousands of people in one local community have had to boil their water for weeks because it may not be safe to drink. Some lost water service for a
by Jaie Avila / News 4 San AntonioThousands of people in one local community have had to boil their water for weeks because it may not be safe to drink.
Some lost water service for a time, followed by low pressure and discolored water. ATASCOSA - Thousands of people in one local community have had to boil their water for weeks because it may not be safe to drink. Some lost water service for a time, followed by low pressure and discolored water.
The Atascosa Rural Water Supply Corp. has four wells, one of them broke down in early May, and in order to fix it, they have to wait for a part that's being shipped from another country. Jorge Johnson doesn't know what to expect when he turns on his faucet. On a good day water comes out with low pressure and leaves gritty particles swirling around the glass.
“I got up to go to work like I normally do, and when I went to turn on the shower, there was no water, absolutely no water," Johnson said. Earlier this month Johnson and his neighbors lost water service and had to drive to a nearby truck stop to take showers.
“It's been a nightmare to say the least. We don't realize how important water is to us, when we've been deprived of it," Johnson said. Back on May 8th a pump failed on one of their wells, and as they were removing it the long pipe that extends hundreds of feet down was damaged.
“It's just one of those things, it was mechanical failure we had no clue it was going to happen," said Mike Fernandez, General Manager of the ARWSC. Fernandez says the replacement pipe had to be shipped from Canada and likely won't arrive until June fifth.
“It's too expensive for anybody in the local area to have 400 feet, they may have twenty, forty, sixty feet somewhere, but not 400 feet, so it had to come from out of state," Fernandez said. Fernandez said the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality told him to issue a boil water notice because it may contain bacteria and metals. But some, like Ray Duque, are disabled and the long delay is frustrating.
“It's critical, you cannot afford for those wells to break down because a lot of people suffer the consequences," Duque said. The water district says it will continue with the boil water notice and providing bottled water to people until they can get that well fixed.
